article_title: Evaluation of a Virtual Laboratory Platform in General Education on Quantum Information Science
citation: Hongbin Song. (2025). Evaluation of a Virtual Laboratory Platform in General Education on Quantum Information Science. General Education Division, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen. https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
title: QLab virtual laboratory platform with a Bell test experiment for undergraduate quantum entanglement learning
description: QLab is a commercially available virtual laboratory platform from Anhui Qasky Quantum Technology Co. Ltd. that "simulates a 3-D physical laboratory environment equipped with various optical devices and instruments", letting undergraduates without experimental expertise conduct a Bell test. The virtual experimental setup consists of three units: generation of a quantum entangled state, distribution of entangled photons, and measurement of quantum correlations. A guidebook outlining principles and operational procedures was distributed in advance, and platform fidelity was ensured through repeated testing.
requirements: A guidebook outlining the principles and operational procedures of the virtual experiment distributed to students in advance
Detailed instructor explanation of each optical device's function in theory before starting the experiment
constraints: Conducting such complex quantum experiments in a real laboratory is impractical for undergraduates due to limitations in equipment and experimental skills, which the virtual platform addresses
target_learners: undergraduates from diverse academic backgrounds, both science and arts, in general education courses
target_learning_goals: understanding the counterintuitive concept of quantum entanglement and the Bell test
examples: Students conducted the Bell test individually in 2022–2023 and 2023–2024, then collaboratively in groups in 2024–2025 during a two-hour tutorial session
